output_text:
Introduction/Context  
A prospective endometrial carcinoma (EC) cohort (CNV-L subgroup) was profiled by global proteomics to compare tumors harboring CTNNB1 hotspot mutations versus CTNNB1 wild-type (WT). Differential analysis of 10,150 quantified proteins (NIHMS1921121-Supplement 7) revealed that CTNNB1 itself and multiple canonical Wnt pathway components were significantly elevated in CTNNB1-mutant tumors. In orthogonal phosphoproteomic data (not shown), CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in mutant tumors, whereas non-hotspot phosphosites trended up.

• AXIN1: L2FC 0.672; FDR 1.89 × 10⁻¹² (up in hotspot)  
• DKK4: L2FC 4.05; FDR 6.39 × 10⁻⁸ (up)

Balanced Analysis  
Across databases, protein-processing/RNA metabolism modules are strongly up in CTNNB1-mutant tumors (e.g., ER protein folding, ribosome and rRNA processing, mitochondrial gene expression, oxidative phosphorylation, Myc targets), reflecting heightened proteostatic and translational activity. Downregulated processes cluster in cell-surface/adhesion modules (complement/coagulation, focal adhesion, cilium assembly, EMT, inflammatory response) consistent with epithelial reprogramming. Wnt pathway–related terms (Basal cell carcinoma, Wnt signaling components) did not reach statistical significance at FDR ≤ 0.05.  

Targeted Subset (Wnt/CTNNB1)  
No pathway term containing “Wnt” or “CTNNB” meets FDR ≤ 0.05 in the GSEA results.  

Key Genes/Proteins (Differential Proteomics)  
Upregulated in CTNNB1 hotspot vs. WT:  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                                   | Pathway(s)        |
|---------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| CTNNB1  | Up (L2FC 0.760; FDR 1.72 × 10⁻¹¹) | β-catenin adherens junction component, transcriptional co-activator | Wnt signaling     |
| AXIN1   | Up (L2FC 0.672; FDR 1.89 × 10⁻¹²) | Scaffold for β-catenin destruction complex      | Wnt signaling     |

Downregulated (Phosphosite)  
| Feature           | Direction | Role/Function                     | Pathway(s)        |
|-------------------|-----------|-----------------------------------|-------------------|
| CTNNB1 S45 phospho | Down      | Regulatory phosphorylation site   | β-catenin turnover |

Comparisons & Implications  
• Proteomic upregulation of CTNNB1 and AXIN1 aligns with CTNNB1 hotspot-driven Wnt activation and protein stabilization.  
• Loss of S45 phosphorylation likely prevents β-catenin degradation, reinforcing nuclear signaling.  
• Downregulation of adhesion/inflammatory modules may reflect epithelial reprogramming and immune exclusion in CTNNB1-mutant EC.  
• Therapeutically, targeting β-catenin stabilization or downstream Wnt effectors may counteract CTNNB1-driven tumorigenesis.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate CTNNB1 and AXIN1 protein abundance and subcellular localization by IHC or subcellular fractionation.  
2. Functionally assess the impact of S45 dephosphorylation on β-catenin stability and transcriptional activity.  
3. Examine expression of canonical Wnt target genes (e.g., AXIN2, MYC) by RNA-seq or qPCR.  
4. Investigate changes in cell adhesion and immune markers (e.g., E-cadherin, CD8) to link pathway shifts to tumor microenvironment.
